description: Fires a tag only after all triggers in the group have been activated the number of times you set. It connects several visitor actions and waits until they all happen before the tag fires. Once the group is activated, extra activations of any trigger won't fire the tag again; the group activates again after page reload. You cannot add one trigger group to another. Multiplicity is set per trigger in the group (e.g. Page view – 1 time, Click – 2 times), not on the group itself. See Piwik PRO help: Trigger group.

trigger_group_creation.note: The trigger group is created with trigger_type 'trigger_group' in attributes, plus member triggers on the top-level MCP relationships.triggers array. Each member object that includes meta must set meta.firing_threshold (>= 1).

attributes.name: Trigger name
attributes.conditions: Required by API. Array of event condition objects (Page URL, Page path, etc.); use [] if no event conditions. Each condition needs condition_id, variable_id, condition_type, value, options.

triggers.description: MCP top-level relationships.triggers: array of UUID strings and/or { id, meta: { firing_threshold } } (firing_threshold >= 1 when meta is present). Sent as JSON:API relationships.triggers.data with type trigger on each item.

wire_triggers_data.description: Wire JSON:API relationships.triggers.data items include id, type: trigger, and optional meta.firing_threshold.

before_you_start: Create the triggers you want to add to the group before creating the trigger group.
You cannot add one trigger group to another trigger group.
trigger_group_creation.mcp_payload_note: Use triggers_create(app_id, attributes, relationships) or triggers_update. Put name, trigger_type, conditions, and other trigger fields only in attributes. Member triggers go only on the top-level relationships object under relationships.triggers: an array of UUID strings and/or { "id": "<uuid>", "meta": { "firing_threshold": <int>=1 } }. The MCP server expands these to JSON:API data.relationships. No other keys are allowed on relationships.

when_to_use: Fire a tag only after multiple actions have happened (e.g. page view + 2 clicks)
Sequence-based conversion (e.g. visit contact page once and click submit twice)
Combine several triggers with different activation counts
common_use_cases: Contact page visit + contact form click (e.g. page view 1 time, click 1 time)
Product page view + add to cart (page view 1, click 1)
Multiple clicks on the same or different elements before firing
best_practices: Create all member triggers first, then create the trigger group with top-level relationships; set meta.firing_threshold on each item in relationships.triggers
Each trigger in the array has its own meta.firing_threshold (e.g. 1 for page view, 2 for click); the group has no separate multiplicity
Do not nest trigger groups inside another trigger group

relationships.description: On MCP tools, pass member triggers via top-level relationships.triggers: an array of UUID strings and/or objects { id, meta: { firing_threshold } } (threshold >= 1). The server converts these to JSON:API relationships.triggers.data with type "trigger" on each item.

meta.firing_threshold: Activation count for this trigger (e.g. 1 or 2)

relationships.recommendation: Include each member trigger once in the array; set meta.firing_threshold on each item.

conditions.description: Required by API. Array of event condition objects; use [] if none. When non-empty, each needs variable_id, condition_type, value, options (condition_id is auto-generated).

trigger_group_page_and_click.description: Fire tag after page view once and click twice. Use top-level relationships for member triggers (MCP convenience array); attributes holds only name, trigger_type, and conditions.

trigger_group_with_event_conditions.description: Trigger group with event conditions; member triggers on top-level relationships.

attributes.name: Product Page View + Add to Cart

common_mistakes: Adding one trigger group as a member of another trigger group (not allowed)
Forgetting to set meta.firing_threshold on each object in relationships.triggers when using per-link meta
Creating the trigger group before creating the member triggers
Expecting the group to have its own multiplicity rule (multiplicity is per trigger via firing_threshold)

possible_causes: Member triggers not yet created or wrong IDs in relationships
meta.firing_threshold missing on one or more items in relationships.triggers when using per-link meta
debugging_steps: Verify all member triggers exist; each object in relationships.triggers must have id and, when meta is used, meta.firing_threshold >= 1
When using per-link meta on a member object, ensure meta.firing_threshold is set and is >= 1
